blockFields: `slis` (list of `{ "name", "good" (the metric or query counting good events), "valid" (the metric or query counting valid events) }`), `measured` (object: `availability28d` as a percentage with two decimals, `latencyP99Ms` over the 28 days), `slos` (list of `{ "sli", "target" (percentage), "windowDays" }`), `alerts` (list of `{ "name", "sli", "burnRate", "longWindowMin", "shortWindowMin", "action" ("page" or "ticket") }`).
kindExtra: Seed: 28 days of per-minute request counts by status class and latency buckets for one API (CSV), with health-check and synthetic traffic mixed in (labelled in a column) that must be excluded; one known bad day; a dependency's published SLO in a vendor note that caps what this API can promise; the metrics catalogue. Key shape: `number` items for the measured availability (tolerance 0.05 points) and p99 (tolerance 5%), computed over real user traffic only (a second wrong value for all traffic must fail, so make the synthetic share large enough to move the number); `every` items on `slis` that good and valid are built from metric names in the catalogue (`inSet`); a `some` item on `slos` with a target at or below the dependency cap and at or below the measured value; `some` items on `alerts` for a fast burn page (burn rate at least 10, long window at most 60 minutes, a short window) and a slow burn ticket (burn rate at most 6, long window at least 360 minutes); a `none` item for alerts on CPU or memory. 12 to 16 items.
brief: Phase: NFR and performance. Role: SRE. Folder: the ops folder of a payments API: 28 days of traffic and latency data, the metrics catalogue, the current alerts (CPU and error-rate pages that fire a lot), a vendor note on the card network dependency, the product team's wish ("five nines"), and an incident list. The request: set the API's availability and latency objectives from the data, and replace the noisy alerts with ones tied to those objectives.

items.text: Says which traffic is left out and why, and how the indicator is computed from the raw counts so someone else can reproduce the number.
items.source: Google SRE workbook, Implementing SLOs, https://sre.google/workbook/implementing-slos/ (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; idea only)

items.text: Explains to the product team, in budget minutes and the dependency's own promise, why the wished-for target cannot be met.
items.source: Google SRE workbook, Implementing SLOs, https://sre.google/workbook/implementing-slos/ (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; idea only)

items.text: Explains how the chosen burn rates and windows trade time to detect against false pages, with the budget spent before each alert fires.
items.source: Google SRE workbook, Alerting on SLOs, https://sre.google/workbook/alerting-on-slos/ (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; idea only)

items.text: States what the team does when the error budget is spent (for example slow feature releases) and who agrees to it.
